Functionality: List loan products for the tenant, ordered by Code
Create a loan product - Code and Name are required
Amount limits are validated: MinAmount/MaxAmount cannot be negative and Min cannot exceed Max
Tenure limits are validated: MinTenureMonths/MaxTenureMonths must be >=1 and Min cannot exceed Max
Product Code is trimmed and must be unique per tenant, else Conflict
Creating a product auto-generates one open-ended Active LoanProductVersion effective from today, carrying the same terms
Update requires the product to exist in the tenant (NotFound) and re-checks code uniqueness excluding itself (Conflict)

Update never touches LoanProductVersions - the product header's own Min/Max amount and tenure fields (used later as CreateLoanAsync's eligibility bounds) and each version's own independently-set Min/Max fields can drift out of sync
CreateProductVersionAsync validates EffectiveTo>=EffectiveFrom, non-negative/ordered amount and tenure bounds, and non-negative InterestRate
A new Active version's date range cannot overlap an existing Active version's range for the same product, else Conflict
LoanProductVersionStatus.Retired is a declared lifecycle state that no service method ever assigns - a version can never be explicitly retired through the API
CreateLoanAsync requires RequestedAmount>0 and RequestedTenureMonths>0, else Invalid
The referenced loan product must exist in the tenant and be Active, else NotFound
The target employee must exist in the tenant, else NotFound - CreateLoanAsync does not additionally require the employee's own Status to be Active, unlike Payroll Run population eligibility
RequestedAmount must fall within the product header's MinAmount/MaxAmount (when set), else Invalid
RequestedTenureMonths must fall within the product header's MinTenureMonths/MaxTenureMonths (when set), else Invalid
MaxConcurrentLoans is stored on the product but is never read or enforced anywhere in CreateLoanAsync - an employee may hold unlimited concurrent loans against a product declaring a cap

The loan's interest terms (InterestMethod/InterestRate) and RecoveryPolicy are resolved from the currently-effective Active LoanProductVersion (latest EffectiveFrom<=today, EffectiveTo null or >=today); when none resolves, the request still succeeds falling back to the product-header InterestMethod/InterestRate/RecoveryPolicy with LoanProductVersionId left at Guid.Empty
LoanNumber is generated as {LN|ADV}/{year}/{random-GUID-fragment} truncated to 22 characters and upper-cased - not a deterministic sequential number
Status resolves to Draft when the product requires approval (default), or straight to Approved (with ApprovedAmount/ApprovedTenureMonths pre-filled from the request) when the product does not
OutstandingPrincipal and OutstandingTotal are pre-populated to RequestedAmount at creation time, before any approval has happened

Creating a loan appends a Created LoanHistory row, and the ESS self-service create route (POST /api/me/loans) forcibly overwrites the submitted EmployeeId with the caller's own linked-employee id before calling CreateLoanAsync
Submit transitions a loan from Draft to Submitted only, else Conflict
Approve requires the loan to be Submitted, else Conflict

Approve invokes PayrollApprovalGuard maker-checker and rejects self-approval when the tenant's PayrollControlConfiguration has RequireMakerChecker and PreventSelfApproval enabled and the approver is the original requester
Approve accepts optional approvedAmount/approvedTenureMonths overrides, defaulting to the originally requested values when omitted
Approve resets OutstandingPrincipal and OutstandingTotal to the (possibly overridden) ApprovedAmount and stamps ApprovedAtUtc/ApprovedByUserId
Reject is allowed from EITHER Submitted or Draft status (not Submitted-only) and requires a non-blank reason, else Invalid

Reject does NOT invoke PayrollApprovalGuard at all - unlike Approve and Cancel, a self-requester can reject their own loan even under a maker-checker/self-approval policy, and RequireReasonForCancellation-style policy reasons never apply to Reject
A loan already Approved, Rejected, Disbursed/Active, Closed or Cancelled cannot be Submitted again
A cross-tenant loan id (submit/approve/reject) is NotFound, not Forbidden
Every submit/approve/reject transition appends an append-only LoanHistory row carrying the previous and next status
RecordDisbursementAsync requires the loan to be Approved, else Conflict
Disbursed amount defaults to ApprovedAmount, must be >0 and cannot exceed ApprovedAmount - a disbursed amount below the approved amount (partial disbursement) is accepted
Disbursement moves the loan to Active and stamps DisbursedAtUtc, appending both Disbursed and Activated LoanHistory events
The installment schedule (BuildSchedule) is generated exactly once per loan, double-guarded by a hadSchedule check before persistence and an internal early-return when installments already exist
InterestMethod.None produces a zero-interest schedule - principal split evenly across the tenure, with the final installment absorbing any rounding remainder

InterestMethod.Flat computes total interest as Principal*Rate%*(TenureMonths/12), split evenly per installment, with principal likewise split evenly and the remainder absorbed by the final installment
InterestMethod.ReducingBalance computes a standard amortizing EMI from the monthly rate and tenure, with each installment's principal component derived from the prior installment's closing balance
Each installment persists OpeningPrincipal/PrincipalAmount/InterestAmount/InstallmentAmount/ClosingPrincipal and a DueDate of the disbursement date advanced by its installment number in months
After disbursement, OutstandingInterest and OutstandingTotal are recomputed as the sum of the generated installments' InterestAmount plus the disbursed principal
GetScheduleAsync returns the persisted installment set ordered by InstallmentNumber, NotFound for an unknown or cross-tenant loan id

The EmployeeLoanDto returned by every read/mutation endpoint embeds the full ordered installment schedule inline, so /api/me/loans/{id} already exposes an ESS employee's own schedule without a separate self-service history/schedule route

LoanPayrollRecoveryResolver.ResolveAsync selects due installments for Active loans only (Status Scheduled or PartiallyRecovered, DueDate<=payDate, RecoveredAmount<InstallmentAmount), ordered by the owning product's RecoveryPriority, then DueDate, then InstallmentNumber

During calculation, the engine adds one LOAN-{loanNumber} deduction PayrollResultComponent per due installment returned by the resolver, tagged CalculationSource=LoanRecovery with loan/installment traceability
RecoveryPolicy.DeferInstallment skips the installment entirely for that payroll cycle - it remains Scheduled/PartiallyRecovered, un-recovered, with no calculation error
RecoveryPolicy.RecoverFullOrFail fails the entire employee's payroll calculation (CalculationFailed) when the installment's TotalDue exceeds the employee's available net pay at that point
RecoveryPolicy.PartialRecovery clips the recovered amount down to whatever net pay remains (floored at zero) instead of failing the calculation
Multiple due installments across multiple loans for the same employee are applied in RecoveryPriority order, each one decrementing the running NetPay before the next is evaluated

On a successful calculation, PersistLoanRecoveriesAsync creates one LoanRepayment (RepaymentType.Payroll) per recovered installment and updates the LoanInstallment's RecoveredAmount/Status/PayrollRunId/PayrollResultId/RecoveredAtUtc
Persisting a payroll recovery is idempotent per (LoanInstallmentId, PayrollResultId) - a recalculation of the same result does not double-record the LoanRepayment
An installment's Status becomes Recovered once RecoveredAmount>=InstallmentAmount, otherwise PartiallyRecovered
Payroll recovery correctly decrements the loan's own OutstandingPrincipal/OutstandingInterest/OutstandingTotal aggregate fields (not only the installment's own RecoveredAmount)

CONFIRMED DEFECT - a loan whose OutstandingTotal is driven to exactly zero purely through payroll-recovery installments is NEVER transitioned to Closed by PersistLoanRecoveriesAsync, unlike RecordRepaymentAsync's manual-repayment path which explicitly closes the loan the moment OutstandingTotal reaches zero; the loan remains Status=Active indefinitely

Group: Repayment, Prepayment, Closure and Outstanding Balance
Functionality: RecordRepaymentAsync (manual repayment) requires the loan to be Active and a positive Amount not exceeding OutstandingTotal, else Conflict/Invalid

Group: Repayment, Prepayment, Closure and Outstanding Balance
Functionality: A manual repayment applies to OutstandingInterest first, then OutstandingPrincipal with the remainder, recording principal/interest split on the LoanRepayment row (RepaymentType.Manual)

Group: Repayment, Prepayment, Closure and Outstanding Balance
Functionality: A manual repayment that drives OutstandingTotal to exactly zero auto-closes the loan (Status=Closed, ClosedAtUtc/ClosedByUserId/ClosureReason stamped)

Group: Repayment, Prepayment, Closure and Outstanding Balance
Functionality: PartialPrepayAsync requires the owning product's AllowPartialPrepayment flag to be enabled, else Conflict

Group: Repayment, Prepayment, Closure and Outstanding Balance
Functionality: PartialPrepayAsync requires the loan to be Active and Amount positive and no greater than OutstandingPrincipal, applying the full amount to principal only (no interest apportionment)

Group: Repayment, Prepayment, Closure and Outstanding Balance
Functionality: INCONSISTENCY - PartialPrepayAsync does NOT auto-close the loan even when the prepayment reduces OutstandingTotal to exactly zero, unlike RecordRepaymentAsync's auto-close-at-zero behavior for the structurally identical scenario

Group: Repayment, Prepayment, Closure and Outstanding Balance
Functionality: A partial prepayment appends a PartialPrepayment LoanHistory row and records a LoanRepayment with RepaymentType.PartialPrepayment

Group: Repayment, Prepayment, Closure and Outstanding Balance
Functionality: CloseAsync (early closure) requires the owning product's AllowEarlyClosure flag, else Conflict, and the loan must be Active

Group: Repayment, Prepayment, Closure and Outstanding Balance
Functionality: A supplied non-zero Amount must exactly equal the loan's current OutstandingTotal, else Invalid with the required amount echoed back in the message; Amount=0 is accepted as shorthand for the current outstanding total

Group: Repayment, Prepayment, Closure and Outstanding Balance
Functionality: Early closure zeroes OutstandingPrincipal/Interest/Total, sets Status=Closed, records a LoanRepayment (RepaymentType.EarlyClosure) for the full outstanding amount, and cancels every remaining Scheduled installment

Group: Repayment, Prepayment, Closure and Outstanding Balance
Functionality: Repayment/prepayment/closure all increment EmployeeLoan.ConcurrencyVersion, a genuine EF IsConcurrencyToken column, so a true concurrent race between two of these actions on the same loan throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException rather than silently double-applying

Group: Repayment, Prepayment, Closure and Outstanding Balance
Functionality: None of the Loan mutation endpoints (repayments/prepay/close/approve/record-disbursement) accept a client-supplied expectedConcurrencyVersion parameter, unlike SalaryComponent/SalaryStructure/EmployeeSalaryAssignment - an ordinary stale-form conflict is caught only by EF's own DbUpdateConcurrencyException (mapped by the global ExceptionHandlingMiddleware to a generic 500), never as a clean, pre-checked 409
Cancel is blocked only when the loan is Active or Closed - every other state (Draft/Submitted/Approved/Rejected/already-Cancelled) is accepted

IDEMPOTENCY GAP - because Cancelled itself is not in the blocked-state list, cancelling an already-Cancelled loan a second time succeeds again, writing a duplicate Cancelled LoanHistory row rather than returning a no-op or Conflict

Cancel invokes PayrollApprovalGuard, so a tenant with RequireReasonForCancellation enabled rejects a Cancel call with a blank reason as Invalid; PreventSelfApproval likewise blocks the original requester from cancelling their own loan under a maker-checker policy
A successful cancellation appends a Cancelled LoanHistory row carrying the previous status and the supplied reason
A cross-tenant loan id on cancel is NotFound, not Forbidden
CalculateSettlementAsync auto-generates one Recovery FinalSettlementLine per Active loan with OutstandingTotal>0 for the settlement's employee, sized to the loan's OutstandingTotal at generation time

Re-running CalculateSettlementAsync (still Draft/Calculated) does not duplicate a loan-recovery line that was already generated for the same loan, but also does not refresh an existing line's Amount if the loan's OutstandingTotal has since changed

On FinalizeSettlementAsync, each EmployeeLoan-sourced line recovers min(line.Amount, loan.OutstandingTotal) - not the possibly-stale line.Amount outright - so a manual repayment made between Calculate and Finalize is correctly reflected and the loan is never over-recovered

Finalization records a LoanRepayment (RepaymentType.FinalSettlement, SourceType=FinalSettlement, Reference=the settlement id) splitting interest/principal from the recovered amount, and idempotently skips a loan line already recovered under the same settlement Reference

Finalization closes the loan (Status=Closed, ClosureReason='Recovered through final settlement.') the moment the recovery brings its OutstandingTotal to zero, and appends a FinalSettlementRecovery LoanHistory row regardless

A loan whose OutstandingTotal exceeds the recorded settlement line's Amount (e.g. a top-up disbursement after Calculate) is only ever recovered up to line.Amount at finalization - the residual outstanding balance survives the settlement and is not separately flagged
A loan that is not Active (e.g. already Closed or Cancelled) at finalization time is silently skipped by its generated settlement line, with no error and no repayment recorded
GetRegisterAsync is a true paged endpoint (Page/PageSize/total count) supporting ProductId/ProductType/EmployeeId/Status/From-To(RequestedAtUtc) filters

LoanRegisterQuery has no registered FluentValidation validator - Page/PageSize are never bounded server-side (no MaxPageSize=100 enforcement, unlike other PagedQuery-derived DTOs in the app), so an oversized PageSize defeats pagination and Page<=0 feeds an unguarded Skip() calculation
Service: PayrollLoanService.cs (full grep for a LoanRegisterQuery validator)

Functionality: The register's per-row NextDueDate is the earliest Scheduled/PartiallyRecovered installment's DueDate, and PrincipalRecovered/InterestRecovered/TotalRecovered are live sums over LoanRepayments rather than stored snapshots

GetLoansAsync (the admin GET /api/payroll/loans listing and every /api/me/loans* ESS route) is NOT paginated at all - it hard-caps at the 500 most-recently-requested loans (OrderByDescending RequestedAtUtc) with no page/pageSize parameters, unlike the true-paged register

There is no dedicated register CSV/export endpoint or reporting sheet for Loans (unlike Payroll Reports/Payroll Analytics/Reimbursements' own Register export) - the design doc itself lists register export as historically deferred scope
CONFIRMED - grep of SeedData.cs's RolePermissionMap shows NO seeded role other than SuperAdmin/TenantAdmin (both via Permissions.All) is granted ANY Payroll.Loans.* permission natively
HRAdmin holds zero Payroll.Loans.* permissions despite natively holding the entire Salary/Structure/Period/Run/Controls/TaxDeclaration/YearEndTax grant list in qa/10-payroll

SuperHR holds zero native Payroll.Loans.* permissions but can self-escalate to full Loans management (View/Request/Approve/Disburse/Recover/Close/Cancel/ManageProducts) via one PageAccess.Manage call, the same CR-66 self-escalation shape documented in qa/06-rbac-account-linking and re-verified in every module since

Employee holds zero Payroll.Loans.* permissions out of the box, including Payroll.Loans.Request - a freshly seeded Employee cannot submit a loan/advance request for themselves through /api/me/loans without an explicit tenant grant

Manager holds zero Payroll.Loans.* permissions - there is no manager/team-scope view of direct reports' loans, consistent with the CR-77 pattern (no team-scope permission concept) already documented for Payroll

Payroll.Loans.Manage and Payroll.Loans.ViewHistory are declared and seeded (ids 147, 153) but checked by zero [HasPermission] attributes anywhere in the codebase - each mutating action is instead gated by its own granular permission and no /history endpoint exists for loans at all

The ESS routes (/api/me/loans*) are gated by the SAME Payroll.Loans.Request permission used for the plain create/submit actions - there is no separate self-view permission, so any role holding Request can also list/read its own linked-employee loans
An unlinked user (no AccountEmployeeLink) calling any /api/me/loans* route receives Unauthorized (No linked employee identity), not an empty result set

MyLoan (GET /api/me/loans/{id}) returns NotFound for a loan id that exists but belongs to a different employee than the caller's own linked identity, even within the same tenant - it never leaks another employee's loan by id
A cross-tenant loan/product id on every read and mutation route (products, loans, register, schedule) is NotFound, not Forbidden - verified across the full TenantId-filter surface
The Loan Register and every admin listing endpoint filter strictly by the resolved tenant - a second tenant's loans/products never appear regardless of query filters supplied

LoanHistory is append-only across the entire lifecycle (Created/Submitted/Approved/Rejected/Disbursed/Activated/PayrollRecovery/ManualRepayment/PartialPrepayment/EarlyClosure/FinalSettlementRecovery/Cancelled) - no update or delete path exists for any LoanHistory row

Every LoanHistory row stamps ActorUserId from the current tenant context and OccurredAtUtc from the injected clock, giving full actor attribution even for system-triggered PayrollRecovery/FinalSettlementRecovery events

There is no exposed GET /history endpoint for a loan despite the append-only LoanHistory table existing and being fully populated - history can only be read directly from the database, not through the API, in contrast with every history-bearing entity in qa/10-payroll
Service: IPayrollLoanService.cs (full grep for a GetHistoryAsync method)

Functionality: A LoanHistory row for a PayrollRecovery or FinalSettlementRecovery event carries SourceType/SourceId pointing back to the originating PayrollResult or FinalSettlementCase, distinguishing system-triggered recovery from a manually-actioned lifecycle change

Group: Concurrency, Provider Parity and Large Data
Functionality: A concurrent early-closure vs. manual-repayment race resolves to exactly one valid lifecycle outcome (Active or Closed), never a corrupted intermediate state
